Khademi, "Why magnetic monopoles are not seen?", International Conference of Mathematical Sciences (Maltepe Üniversitesi, 2009), pp. 365-366, ISBN 9786052124154; Maltepe University open-access repository, hdl:20.500.12415/6128 (now 20.500.12415/2255 in OpenAIRE), CC0; OpenAlex W3153563614 (conference proceedings: a two-page contribution; OpenAIRE marks it nonPeerReviewed)
findings.summary: Explains the non-detection of magnetic monopoles by quantum uncertainty in phase space. The abstract: Maxwell's dual symmetry predicts monopoles, which have not been detected, and Dirac obtained charge quantization from them; the paper shows that 'the uncertainty in the phase space quantum mechanics could be the responsible of the non-visibility of magnetic monopoles'. Read from the repository's own item page as archived by the Wayback Machine (2021-05-10) and from OpenAIRE's harvest of the repository (2026-08-19). The two-page text (371.pdf) could not be retrieved.
findings.difference: Same question as C3 (why monopoles are not seen) and the same kind of agent, position-momentum (phase-space) quantum uncertainty, which C3's own statement uses (an object compact in momentum is spread in position by about hbar/Delta p). The abstract does not say where the monopoles live: no momentum space, conjugate or p-polarized sector, Born reciprocity, dark matter or abundance, and no claim that position-space searches miss objects compact in momentum. Only the two-page text can show whether its argument is C3's mechanism (which would make it partial) or another use of phase-space uncertainty, and it is still unread. Inference, not read: its 'phase space quantum mechanics' is probably the Kirkwood phase-space picture of Khademi and Nasiri 2008 (J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 128, 012016; C4 related in findings.json), which obtains charge quantization without monopoles. The repository lists Khademi alone; round 3's Zanjan faculty listing gives S. Khademi and S. Nasiri for a talk of the same title at the Multiphysics conference, Lille, December 2009 (not checked). It is the closest item to C3 the check has found.

The handle server API resolves hdl 20.500.12415/6128 to openaccess.maltepe.edu.tr/handle/20.500.12415/6128; the repository answers a plain nginx 403 to the landing page, OAI-PMH GetRecord, the DSpace REST API and the PDF bitstream, as on 2026-11-02 (not worked around). The Wayback Machine holds the repository's own item page (DSpace 6.2, capture 2021-05-10, HTTP 200), and OpenAIRE's API returns the same record harvested from the repository (collected 2026-08-19, now under handle 20.500.12415/2255 after a renumbering). Both give the abstract and the metadata: conference object, 'Why magnetic monopoles are not seen?', Siamak Khademi alone, source 'International Conference of Mathematical Sciences', publisher Maltepe Üniversitesi, 2009, pp. 365-366, ISBN 9786052124154, CC0, full text 371.pdf (97.93 KB); OpenAIRE marks it nonPeerReviewed. Abstract, verbatim (FOUND with lit.py's norm() in both copies): 'Dual symmetry of Maxwell’s equations predicts the existence of magnetic monopoles which are not detected until now. As an important consequence of this prediction, the quantization of electric charge is obtained by P.A.M. Dirac. In this paper I show the uncertainty in the phase space quantum mechanics could be the responsible of the non-visibility of magnetic monopoles.' The PDF was never archived (CDX: no bitstream URL). The other routes failed: OpenAlex W3153563614 has one location (the repository), no abstract, closed; CORE gave API 429 and a web bot check; BASE served a JavaScript proof-of-work page; Google Books gave 429 for the ISBN; Semantic Scholar's title match gave 429; two web searches and Maltepe's ICMS proceedings page found no copy and no 2009 volume. Label for C3: related, conservatively. It explains the same null result by phase-space quantum uncertainty, but the abstract does not place the monopoles in momentum space, so C3's 'not found' stands on the abstract. The two-page text could raise the item to partial, and it is still unread.
